title: Nanzhao sacks the Pyu city of Halin
description: An army from Nanzhao in Yunnan destroys the Pyu city, ending a thousand years of Pyu city-states in the Irrawaddy valley.

title: Pagan fortified
description: According to the chronicles King Pyinbya walls the settlement of Pagan, which the Burmans make their capital.

title: Anawrahta takes the throne
description: Anawrahta becomes king of Pagan and goes on to unite the Irrawaddy valley for the first time.

title: Conquest of Thaton
description: Anawrahta takes the Mon kingdom in the south, a conquest the chronicles credit with bringing Theravada Buddhism and Mon learning to Pagan.

title: Ananda Temple built
description: King Kyansittha completes one of the largest and best preserved of the more than two thousand temples of Pagan.

title: Mongols end the Pagan Kingdom
description: After Mongol invasions from Yunnan, King Narathihapate is killed and the kingdom breaks up into small states.

title: Ava founded
description: Thado Minbya founds a capital at the meeting of the Irrawaddy and Myitnge rivers, the seat of Upper Burma for most of the next five centuries.

title: Mrauk U founded
description: King Min Saw Mon founds the capital of an Arakanese kingdom that lasts until 1785.

title: Tabinshwehti takes Pegu
description: The king of Toungoo captures the capital of the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy and moves his court there.

title: Bayinnaung takes Ava
description: Bayinnaung conquers Upper Burma, reuniting the country on the way to building the largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia.

title: Capture of Syriam
description: King Anaukpetlun takes the port from the Portuguese adventurer Filipe de Brito and restores Toungoo rule over the coast.

title: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty
description: After Ava falls to the Mons, a village headman declares himself king and begins the reconquest of the country.

title: Yangon founded
description: Alaungpaya takes the town of Dagon and renames it Yangon, 'end of strife'.

title: Sino-Burmese War
description: Burma defeats four invasions by Qing China, and the war ends with a truce at Kaungton.

title: Treaty of Yandabo
description: The treaty ending the First Anglo-Burmese War gives Britain Arakan, Tenasserim and Assam and imposes a heavy indemnity.

title: Second Anglo-Burmese War
description: Britain seizes Rangoon and annexes Lower Burma, cutting the kingdom off from the sea.

title: Mandalay founded
description: King Mindon founds a new royal capital at the foot of Mandalay Hill, the last capital of the Burmese kings.

title: Fall of Mandalay
description: British troops take the capital in the Third Anglo-Burmese War, King Thibaw is exiled to India and the monarchy ends.

title: Saya San rebellion
description: A peasant revolt against colonial taxes breaks out in the delta and takes the British two years to suppress.

title: Japanese take Rangoon
description: The Japanese army enters the capital and drives the British out of Burma within three months.

title: Panglong Agreement
description: Aung San and Shan, Kachin and Chin leaders agree to join in a single independent Burma with autonomy for the frontier areas.

title: Assassination of Aung San
description: Gunmen kill the independence leader and six members of his cabinet at the Secretariat, six months before independence.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Burma becomes an independent republic outside the Commonwealth, and civil war begins within months.

title: Ne Win's coup
description: General Ne Win overthrows the elected government, beginning half a century of military rule.

title: 8888 Uprising
description: Nationwide protests against one-party rule are crushed by the army, which kills thousands and takes power directly in September.

title: Election result ignored
description: Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy wins about four fifths of the seats, but the military refuses to hand over power.

title: Capital moved to Naypyidaw
description: The military government moves the seat of government from Yangon to a newly built city in the centre of the country.

title: Saffron Revolution
description: Tens of thousands of Buddhist monks lead protests against the military government, which breaks them up by force.

title: Cyclone Nargis
description: The cyclone and its storm surge kill about 138,000 people in the Irrawaddy Delta, the worst natural disaster in the country's history.

title: National League for Democracy wins the election
description: Aung San Suu Kyi's party wins a majority in the first openly contested election since 1990 and forms a government the next year.

title: Rohingya driven from Rakhine
description: After attacks on police posts by Rohingya insurgents, an army campaign of killing and burning drives more than 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh.
